source: RR20/64/64.1–64.2, unchanged authoritative text and printed event/action native evidence reused after hashes
literal_question: How do you identify a district’s tier on the board, and does being in a higher tier inherently change its production or threat?
actual_asked_facts: The number of bars under the district name identifies its tier.
Tier has no inherent effect on production or threat.
contextual_background: Matching district-border color is a supplementary identification aid, not an additional completeness prerequisite.

Printed cards may refer to tiers and impose card-specific tier conditions. This correct explanation is not independently asked by the inherent-effect question; any volunteered false assertion still counts.
scope_verdict: The question asks tier identification and absence of inherent production/threat effects. Printed-card references are a correct explanation, not an additional independently asked fact.

asked_facts: Outages in both higher tiers give five threat only, not eight.
Only tier one gives no upper-half threat increase.
Check upper effect before lower placements.
actual_coverage_elsewhere.procedure: Explicit tier3-over-tier2 conditional priority, tier1-only no upper effect, and upper check before placements.

asked_facts: Riot finds tier-two Human First and adds two threat; Beset finds tier-three and adds four.
Otherwise each Human First moves once, highest-numbered district first; do not apply both branches.
actual_coverage_elsewhere.procedure: Explicit required-tier Human First condition and absent-tier alternative movement branch/order.

asked_facts: Scorched Earth places one outage in a district not already in outage to remove enemies there and in another district in the same tier.
actual_coverage_elsewhere.procedure: Scorched Earth same-tier target geography, independently asked; no SG01 ruling inferred.

locator_precision_advisory.explanation: Q75 asks component/state thresholds and counts, not a tier condition. Do not count Q75 as actual tier-condition coverage. Q71/Q72 directly cover the relevant procedure and Q60 directly covers same-tier targeting, so this overbroad locator introduces no source or procedural gap.

stopping_impact: No changed question, fixed outcome, rule procedure, novelty issue or operative coverage. Reuse the two v10 broad zero-addition passes without claiming new passes or increasing count.
